name: Neolithic Levant
capital: No capital (sites: Göbekli Tepe, Jericho, Çatalhöyük nearby)
summary: The first farming communities of the Fertile Crescent, where people began to grow wheat and barley and herd animals. They built Göbekli Tepe’s carved stone circles and Jericho’s walls, among the oldest monuments and towns on Earth.

location.value: The Levant and Upper Mesopotamia in the Fertile Crescent (modern Turkey, Syria, Israel, Palestine, Jordan, Iraq).

terrain.value: Hilly flanks and river valleys where wild wheat, barley, sheep and goats lived naturally.

climate.value: The warmer, wetter Holocene began around 9700 BCE after the Younger Dryas cold spell, helping early farming.

resources.value: Wild cereals and legumes, flint and obsidian for tools, limestone for building.

disasters.value: A sudden cold, dry event around 6200 BCE (the 8.2-kiloyear event) disrupted many settlements.

population.value: No reliable estimate; villages grew from dozens to a few thousand people.

urbanisation.value: Jericho was settled by about 9000 BCE and is called the “oldest fortified city in the world”.

disease.value: Living close to animals and in crowded villages brought new diseases.

migration.value: Farming spread from here into Anatolia, Europe and Iran over the following millennia.

economicBase.value: The start of farming and herding: domesticated wheat, barley, peas, lentils, sheep and goats (the Neolithic Revolution).

tradeRoutes.value: Obsidian from Anatolia was traded hundreds of kilometres across the region.

wealth.value: No estimate is possible for this period.

moneyAndTax.value: No money; exchange of goods such as obsidian and shells.

inequality.value: Mostly small-scale and fairly equal communities; special buildings suggest some leaders or ritual specialists.

governmentType.value: No states; villages probably organised by kin groups and elders.

keyRulers.value: No rulers are known; there was no writing.

institutions.value: Shared ritual buildings, such as the enclosures at Göbekli Tepe.

stability.value: Settlements lasted centuries, with shifts linked to climate.

armyAndTech.value: Flint-tipped arrows and spears; Jericho’s wall and tower may have been for defence or flood protection.

territoryChange.value: Farming villages spread across the Fertile Crescent.

inventions.value: Plant and animal domestication; some of the world’s oldest known megaliths (Göbekli Tepe pillars).

scienceEducation.value: No writing; knowledge of plants and seasons passed orally.

openness.value: Ideas, seeds and obsidian moved between villages over long distances.

religion.value: Göbekli Tepe’s carved pillars give insights into prehistoric religion; skull cults (plastered skulls) at Jericho.

artsArchitecture.value: Large circular enclosures with T-shaped stone pillars carved with animals (Göbekli Tepe); Jericho’s stone tower.

socialStructure.value: Families and kin groups in villages; plastered skulls suggest ancestor rituals.

sharedIdentity.value: Shared ritual practices across the region.

neighbours.value: Hunter-gatherers of the surrounding steppe and mountains.

ideasReligions.value: Farming and village life spread outwards to Anatolia, Europe and South Asia.

colonisation.value: Farmers moved into new lands, gradually replacing or mixing with hunter-gatherers.

riseSignals.value: Göbekli Tepe was used from about 9500 BCE; early cultivation began.

peakPeriod.value: The PPNB period (8800–6500 BCE), with larger villages and full farming.

declineSignals.value: Abandonment of many large sites around 6500 BCE, possibly due to climate and soil exhaustion.

outcome.value: Followed by the Pottery Neolithic; farming became the way of life across the region.

sources.value: Archaeology (Kenyon at Jericho, Schmidt at Göbekli Tepe). Checked against Wikipedia (“Pre-Pottery Neolithic A”, “Pre-Pottery Neolithic B”, “Göbekli Tepe”, “Jericho”).

overallCertainty.value: Medium. Dates come from radiocarbon dating; the meaning of the monuments is debated. Second source: Wikidata ends the Pre-Pottery Neolithic c. 7000 BCE; this app uses 6500 BCE (end of PPNB).

knownFor.label: Göbekli Tepe pillars
knownFor.note: Carved T-shaped stone pillars, among the oldest known megaliths.

knownFor.label: First wheat and barley farms
knownFor.note: Domestication of the first cereal crops.

knownFor.label: Walls and tower of Jericho
knownFor.note: Early stone defences at one of the oldest towns.

knownFor.label: Plastered skulls
knownFor.note: Human skulls modelled with plaster, possibly for ancestor worship.
